title: Guide - A Thankful Heart - A prayer of thanks

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, steady and unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to A Thankful Heart. <short pause> This is A Prayer of Thanks. <short pause> For the next few minutes, we will simply pray our way through a day, from morning to night. <short pause> I'll lend you some words. <short pause> You can keep the ones that fit.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Come to rest for a moment, wherever this finds you. <short pause> It doesn't matter what time it is. <short pause> A whole day can fit inside a prayer. <short pause> Let your hands be open, if you like... <short pause> and let your breathing become unhurried.

There is a song in the Bible that was written for the Sabbath day, when work was set down, and there was time to look back at what God had done. <short pause> It is Psalm ninety-two. <short pause> This is how it opens, in verses one and two.
It is a good thing to give thanks unto the Lord, and to sing praises unto thy name, O most High: <short pause> To shew forth thy lovingkindness in the morning, and thy faithfulness every night.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Love in the morning. <short pause> Faithfulness every night. <short pause> As if thanks were a thread, tied at both ends of the day, so that nothing in between falls outside of His care. <short pause> Let's follow that thread now, and pray.

Lord of the morning, <short pause> thank You for waking me, on the days I sprang up, and the days I could hardly rise. <short pause> Thank You for the first light, for water on my face, for the first thing I tasted. <short pause> Before I had done one useful thing, I was already loved. <short pause> For Your lovingkindness in the morning... <short pause> I give You thanks.

Lord of the working hours, <short pause> thank You for what my hands are able to do, and for rest when they cannot. <short pause> Thank You for work that mattered, and dull work that fed someone. <short pause> For the mistakes that were forgiven, and the help that came when I didn't know how to ask. <short pause> For strength enough for the middle of the day... <short pause> I give You thanks.

Lord of every table, <short pause> thank You for the people You have set around my life. <short pause> The ones who are easy to love, and the ones who are teaching me how. <short pause> The ones I miss. <short pause> The ones whose names I never learned, who grew my food, and cleaned the floors, and kept watch while I slept. <short pause> For every kindness that reached me through another person... <short pause> I give You thanks.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Pause here, and add one name of your own. <short pause> Someone this prayer would not be complete without. <short pause> Say the name silently... <short pause> and let it rest for a breath in the hands of God. <short pause> For them, Lord... <short pause> I give You thanks.

Lord of the evening, <short pause> thank You for the door that closes behind me, and the work that can wait. <short pause> Thank You for what went well. <short pause> And for what did not, thank You that it does not have the last word. <short pause> You were there in the parts I would live again, and in the parts I would not. <short pause> For Your faithfulness every night... <short pause> I give You thanks.

And Lord of my whole life, <short pause> thank You for what is older than this day. <short pause> For every time You carried me when I only thought I was walking. <short pause> For mercy I did not earn, and for more grace than I could ever count. <short pause> For Jesus, and for the love that will not let me go... <short pause> I give You thanks. <short pause> Amen.

There may be days when you mean every word of that prayer, and days when you can mean only one line. <short pause> Both are prayer. <short pause> It is still a good thing to give thanks... <short pause> however small the voice you bring to it.

Tie the thread at both ends, if you can. <short pause> One thank You when you first open your eyes. <short pause> And one before you close them again. <short pause> The day in between belongs to Him. <short pause> Go with a thankful heart.
